1	# AI Insights
     2	
     3	AI coding agents forget everything between chat sessions. AI Insights fixes that — it gives agents persistent memory, defined roles, and a repeatable pipeline so complex projects survive across sessions without losing context.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## What's Inside
     8	
     9	### Agent Personas
    10	
    11	**Are you here to make your own personas?** [Start Here](https://mistralys.github.io/ai-insights/)
    12	
    13	Each persona is a carefully crafted prompt file that turns a general-purpose AI into a specialist — a code reviewer, a security auditor, a release engineer. Load one in your IDE (VS Code / Claude Code) and the agent knows its job, its boundaries, and how to hand off to the next stage. The system prioritizes robust persona reliability over complex, constantly changing toolsets.
    14	
    15	The following persona suites are available:
    16	
    17	| Suite | Description | Docs |
    18	|-------|-------------|------|
    19	| **Ledger** | Full 9-stage workflow (Planner → PM → Developer → QA → Security → Reviewer → Release → Docs → Synthesis) with persistent state via the MCP server | [personas/ledger/README.md](personas/ledger/README.md) |
    20	| **Ledger Support** | Utility agents that extend the ledger workflow — PM sub-agents, ledger doctor, orchestrator runner, and more | [personas/ledger-support/README.md](personas/ledger-support/README.md) |
    21	| **Standalone** | Drop-in agents with no dependencies — pick one and go | [personas/standalone/](personas/standalone/) |
    22	
    23	### Skills
    24	
    25	Reusable AI agent workflows that can be invoked directly from VS Code (via GitHub Copilot) or Claude Code. Skills delegate to a named persona at runtime — for example, the `insights-audit-persona` skill launches the Persona Curator in Audit mode to evaluate a persona against the Persona Design Guide.
    26	
    27	Source files live in `skills/`. Build output goes to `dist/vscode-skills/` and `dist/claude-skills/` (gitignored). To build and deploy:
    28	
    29	```bash
    30	node scripts/build-skills.js           # compile to dist/
    31	node scripts/build-skills.js --check   # verify only (no files written)
    32	node scripts/publish-skills.js         # deploy to .github/skills/ and ~/.claude/skills/
    33	```
    34	
    35	→ [skills/README.md](skills/README.md) — adding skills, metadata fields, output layout, and runtime dependencies
    36	
    37	### The Project Ledger
    38	
    39	The reason agents can pick up where the last one left off. This [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) stores project state — work packages, progress, handoff notes — so every agent in the pipeline sees the full history. A built-in knowledge store captures insights across runs, giving your agents institutional memory that grows over time.
    40	
    41	→ [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md)
    42	
    43	### The Orchestrator
    44	
    45	Run the entire 9-stage pipeline from the command line — no IDE required. Built on **LangGraph** + **Deep Agents**, the orchestrator executes the same MCP-backed workflow headlessly. Useful for automation, CI integration, or when you want to kick off a pipeline and walk away.
    46	
    47	→ [orchestrator/README.md](orchestrator/README.md)
    48

    53	- **Node.js** >= 18
    54	- **Python 3.11+** (only for the orchestrator)

1	# Model Registry
     2	
     3	The `model-registry/` directory holds the file-based model configuration for the persona system. It contains three files with distinct lifecycles:
     4	
     5	| File | Tracked in Git | Purpose |
     6	|---|---|---|
     7	| `default.json` | ✅ Yes | Shipped seed models. Copied into `local.json` on first access. |
     8	| `local.json` | ❌ No (gitignored) | Working copy of the model list. Single source of truth at runtime. |
     9	| `assignments.json` | ❌ No (gitignored) | Per-persona model assignments and the global default model selection. |
    10	
    11	## How `default.json` and `local.json` Relate
    12	
    13	`default.json` is a **seed file**, not a runtime layer. It exists solely so new installations start with a sensible set of models. At runtime:
    14	
    15	1. On first access, `local.json` is auto-initialized by copying all entries from `default.json`.
    16	2. The GUI's **Load Defaults** button re-runs this merge on demand — new default entries (identified by `id`) are added to `local.json`; entries that already exist are left unchanged.
    17	3. Once copied into `local.json`, entries are fully editable and deletable like any user-registered model.
    18	
    19	There is no concept of "built-in" vs. "custom" at runtime — `local.json` is the single source of truth for the model list. `default.json` is never read during normal operation.
    20	
    21	## Entry Schema
    22	
    23	Each entry in `default.json` (and `local.json`) is a JSON object with exactly four fields:
    24	
    25	| Field | Type | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `id` | UUID string | Stable primary key. Never changes after creation — even if `name` or `slug` is edited. |
    28	| `name` | string | Human-readable display name (shown in the GUI). |
    29	| `slug` | string | URL-safe identifier used internally for model resolution. |
    30	| `cc_model` | string | Claude Code model value. See [cc_model values](#cc_model-values) below. |
    31	
    32	### `cc_model` Values
    33	
    34	- **`"inherit"`** — Claude Code defers to the user's configured model. Use this for Anthropic models, where Claude Code's built-in `inherit` behaviour is appropriate.
    35	- **Explicit model name** (e.g., `"gemini-3-5-flash"`) — Use this for non-Anthropic models that Claude Code cannot resolve via `inherit`.
    36	
    37	## Formatting Convention
    38	
    39	Entries in `default.json` use **single-line inline JSON**, one object per line, with fields in the order `id`, `name`, `slug`, `cc_model`. This keeps diffs minimal (one line changed per entry) and makes the file easy to scan:
    40	
    41	```json
    42	[
    43	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "name": "Inherit / Auto", "slug": "inherit", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    44	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001", "name": "Claude Opus 4.6", "slug": "claude-opus-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    45	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002", "name": "Claude Sonnet 4.6", "slug": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "cc_model": "inherit" },
    46	  { "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003", "name": "Gemini 3.5 Flash", "slug": "gemini-3-5-flash", "cc_model": "gemini-3-5-flash" }
    47	]
    48	```
    49	
    50	Maintain this convention when adding new default entries so that `git diff` output remains readable.
    51	
    52	## Deterministic Zero-Namespace UUIDs
    53	
    54	Default entries use **deterministic zero-namespace UUIDs** — sequential values starting at `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`. This is intentional:
    55	
    56	- **Stable across installations** — the same UUID always refers to the same default model, regardless of when or where the workspace was cloned.
    57	- **Safe merge-by-ID in `loadDefaults()`** — when loading defaults into `local.json`, the merge logic matches entries by `id`. Deterministic UUIDs guarantee that the "Inherit / Auto" entry (id `000...000`) or "Claude Sonnet 4.6" (id `000...002`) can never accidentally collide with a user-generated entry (which uses randomly-generated UUIDs).
    58	
    59	When adding a new default model to `default.json`, assign the next sequential zero-namespace UUID (e.g., `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004`).
    60	
    61	## The "Inherit / Auto" Sentinel
    62	
    63	The first entry — slug `inherit`, id `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — is a **sentinel value**. When a persona is assigned this model:
    64	
    65	- **VS Code output:** The `model` frontmatter field is omitted entirely (the user's model picker selection takes effect).
    66	- **Claude Code output:** `model: 'inherit'` is set in frontmatter (Claude Code defers to the user's configured model).
    67	- **Orchestrator:** Skips the assignment and falls back to YAML-based resolution.
    68	
    69	Consumers identify the sentinel by checking `slug === 'inherit'` on the resolved slug — no special-case structure is needed in assignment storage.
    70	
    71	## Adding a New Default Model
    72	
    73	1. Open `default.json`.
    74	2. Append a new entry at the end of the array using the next sequential zero-namespace UUID.
    75	3. Set `cc_model` to `"inherit"` for Anthropic models, or to the explicit model name for non-Anthropic models.
    76	4. Follow the single-line inline JSON formatting convention.
    77	5. The new entry will be merged into existing `local.json` files the next time **Load Defaults** is triggered from the GUI.
    78	
    79	## Further Reading
    80	
    81	- [Personas Build System](../README.md) — Overview of the template engine and suite structure
    82	- [Plan: Model Settings](../../docs/agents/plans/2026-07-21-model-settings/plan.md) — Architecture decisions and rationale for the model registry design

   114	
   115	| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
   116	|----------|----------|---------|-------------|
   117	| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | one of | — | API key for Anthropic Chat models |

   120	| `CHECKPOINT_DIR` | no | `./checkpoints` | Directory for LangGraph SQLite checkpoint files |
   121	| `LOG_LEVEL` | no | `INFO` | Python logging verbosity |
   122	| `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S` | no | `120` | Seconds of console silence before emitting an "alive" heartbeat (`0` = disabled) |

   124	| `STREAM_MAX_RETRIES` | no | `2` | Maximum retry attempts on transient API errors mid-stream (overloaded, rate-limited, 5xx, network). `0` disables retry entirely. Invalid or non-numeric values fall back to the default. |

   126

At startup, `load_config()` calls `extract_persona_model_slugs()` to build the `stage_models` map — one model slug per stage — sourced from `model_slug` (per-persona) or `default_model_slug` (from `_shared.yaml`). The provider is **auto-detected** from which API key is set (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for `claude-*` slugs, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` for `gemini-*` slugs). `MODEL_NAME` is not read and has no effect.
   128	
   129	---
   130	
   131	## Usage
   132	
   133	### Running via the CLI Menu (Recommended)
   134	
   135	From the workspace root, use the interactive menu for all orchestrator operations:
   136	
   137	```bash
   138	./menu.sh          # macOS / Linux
   139	menu.cmd           # Windows
   140	```
   141	
   142	Or invoke commands directly:
   143	
   144	```bash
   145	./menu.sh preflight                     # verify environment readiness
   146	./menu.sh preflight --plan path/to/plan.md  # also verify plan file exists
   147	./menu.sh orchestrator path/to/plan.md  # launch a run
   148	./menu.sh kill-orchestrator             # terminate stale processes
   149	./menu.sh preview-prompts               # render stage prompts for review
   150	./menu.sh preview-prompts --list        # list available stages
   151	```
   152	
   153	The menu's orchestrator launcher performs a **build freshness check** — if `mcp-server/src/` is newer than `mcp-server/dist/`, it rebuilds automatically before starting. This prevents silent failures from a stale compiled server. You never need to manually rebuild.
   154	
   155	> **Note:** Orchestrator runs can also be launched from the **GUI dashboard** (`./menu.sh gui` → Orchestrator tab) — including preflight checks, run monitoring, and log browsing — all without touching the command line.
   156	
   157	> **Pre-requisite:** Your Python virtual environment must be activated so that `orchestrate` is on `PATH`. Run `source orchestrator/.venv/bin/activate` (or the Windows equivalent) before invoking the menu.
   158	
   159	### Common examples
   160	
   161	```bash
   162	# Override iteration limit
   163	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --max-iterations 50
   164	
   165	# Override the target project path
   166	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --project-path /path/to/my-project
   167	
   168	# Dry run (prints routing decisions without calling agents)
   169	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --dry-run
   170	
   171	# Resume a previous run from the last checkpoint
   172	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --resume <thread-id>
   173	
   174	# Pause for human review before specific stages
   175	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --interrupt-on pm,fail,synthesis
   176	
   177	# Verbose logging
   178	./menu.sh orchestrator plan.md --log-level DEBUG
   179	```
   180	
   181	### Direct invocation (Advanced)
   182	
   183	If you prefer to bypass the menu, you can call `orchestrate` directly:
   184	
   185	```bash
   186	orchestrate path/to/plan.md
   187	orchestrate plan.md --dry-run
   188	```
   189	
   190	Or via the raw scripts (advanced — only when you need full control):
   191	
   192	```bash
   193	node scripts/run-orchestrator.js path/to/plan.md
   194	node scripts/preflight-orchestrator.js --check-api-key
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Developer utilities
   198	
   199	#### Previewing stage prompts
   200	
   201	`scripts/preview-prompts.py` renders all orchestrator stage prompt templates with representative placeholder values and writes the fully-resolved Markdown files to `orchestrator/dist/stage-prompts/` (gitignored). Use it to inspect the exact prompt each stage will receive.
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	# Via the CLI menu (recommended)
   205	./menu.sh preview-prompts
   206	./menu.sh preview-prompts --stage developer
   207	./menu.sh preview-prompts --list
   208	```
   209	
   210	Direct invocation (advanced):
   211	
   212	```bash
   213	node scripts/cli.js preview-prompts
   214	python scripts/preview-prompts.py --stage reviewer
   215	python scripts/preview-prompts.py --list
   216	```
   217	
   218	No `.env` file or LLM credentials are required — the script imports only `prompt_renderer` and the Python standard library.
   219	
   220	---
   221	
   222	### Locating a run's thread ID
   223	
   224	The thread ID is printed at the start of every run and in the run summary under `Thread ID`. It looks like a UUID: `3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6`.
   225	
   226	### Resume safety: terminal checkpoint guard
   227	
   228	When a run completes successfully without `--interrupt-on`, the orchestrator writes a `{thread_id}.terminal` marker file in the checkpoint directory. Attempting to `--resume` a terminal thread ID exits immediately with an error:
   229	
   230	```
   231	orchestrate: error: thread '3fa85f64-...' is a completed run
   232	  (terminal checkpoint — nothing left to execute).
   233	  To start a fresh run, omit --resume.
   234	```
   235	
   236	Runs that stop at an `--interrupt-on` breakpoint are **not** marked terminal so they can be stepped and resumed normally.
   237	
   238	### Signal handling and resumable interrupts
   239	
   240	On Unix (Linux, macOS) the orchestrator registers handlers for **SIGTERM** and **SIGINT** using `loop.add_signal_handler()`. When a signal is received:
   241	
   242	1. The running graph task is cancelled cleanly.
   243	2. A `signal_shutdown` JSONL entry is written (`result: "INTERRUPTED"`).
   244	3. The process exits with code `1`.
   245	
   246	Because no terminal marker is written, a signal-interrupted run **can be resumed** from its last LangGraph checkpoint:
   247	
   248	```bash
   249	# Interrupted run — thread ID is printed at run start and in the summary
   250	orchestrate plan.md --resume <thread-id>
   251	```
   252	
   253	On **Windows**, `loop.add_signal_handler()` is unavailable. The handler falls back to `signal.signal()` for SIGTERM (a no-op on Windows but harmless), and SIGINT continues to be handled by the existing `KeyboardInterrupt` path.
   254	
   255	### Run metadata file (`.orchestrator-run.json`)
   256	
   257	Each time `orchestrate` runs against a plan directory, it writes a
   258	`.orchestrator-run.json` file **inside the plan directory** (next to `plan.md`).
   259	The file is created immediately after the thread ID is resolved — before graph
   260	execution begins — so external tools (e.g., the GUI sidecar) can detect an
   261	in-progress run without parsing the JSONL log. All writes are atomic (temp file
   262	+ `os.replace()`) so the file is never left partially written. It is listed in
   263	`.gitignore`.
   264	
   265	#### Schema
   266	
   267	| Field | Type | Description |
   268	|-------|------|-------------|
   269	| `thread_id` | `string` | LangGraph thread ID (UUID) for this run. |
   270	| `plan_path` | `string` | Absolute resolved path to the `plan.md` file. |
   271	| `slug` | `string` | Plan directory name (basename of the plan directory). |
   272	| `started_at` | `string` | ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of run start. |
   273	| `is_resume` | `boolean` | `true` when the run was launched with `--resume`. |
   274	| `dry_run` | `boolean` | `true` when the run was launched with `--dry-run`. |
   275	| `log_filename` | `string` | Basename of the JSONL log file for this run. |
   276	| `pid` | `integer` | OS process ID of the orchestrator process. |
   277	| `result` | `string \| null` | Run outcome once complete; `null` while in progress. Valid values: `"SUCCESS"`, `"INTERRUPTED"`, `"ERROR"`. |
   278	| `error` | `string \| null` | Error message when `result` is `"ERROR"`; `null` otherwise. |
   279	| `duration_s` | `number \| null` | Wall-clock duration in seconds; `null` while in progress. |
   280	
   281	#### Lifecycle
   282	
   283	```
   284	Run starts
   285	  → result: null, error: null, duration_s: null
   286	
   287	Completes successfully
   288	  → result: "SUCCESS", duration_s: <seconds>
   289	
   290	Paused at --interrupt-on breakpoint, or SIGTERM/SIGINT received
   291	  → result: "INTERRUPTED", duration_s: <seconds>
   292	
   293	Error during execution
   294	  → result: "ERROR", error: "<message>", duration_s: <seconds>
   295	
   296	--resume called on a terminal (already-completed) thread ID
   297	  → result: "ERROR", error: "<message>", duration_s: 0.0  (written before exit)
   298	```
   299	
   300	Starting a new run against the same plan directory overwrites the file with fresh data.

301	
   302	---
   303	
   304	## Architecture
   305	
   306	```
   307	                        ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
   308	                        │             LangGraph graph           │
   309	                        │                                       │
   310	          START ──────→ │  supervisor (router — no LLM call)    │
   311	                        │       │                               │
   312	                        │       │  Command(goto=...)            │
   313	                        │       ↓                               │
   314	                        │  pm ──────────────────────────────┐   │
   315	                        │  developer ────────────────────── │   │
   316	                        │  qa ───────────────────────────── │   │
   317	                        │  security_auditor ─────────────── │─────supervisor
   318	                        │  reviewer ─────────────────────── │   │
   319	                        │  release_engineer ─────────────── │   │
   320	                        │  docs ─────────────────────────── ┘   │
   321	                        │                                       │
   322	                        │  synthesis ─────────────────────→ END │
   323	                        └───────────────────────────────────────┘
   324	```
   325	
   326	### Supervisor (deterministic router)
   327	
   328	The supervisor is a pure-Python deterministic router — **no LLM calls** are made here. All routing is delegated to the MCP server's `ledger_get_next_action` tool, making the ledger the single source of truth for workflow progression. `ledger_get_project_status` is called for observability. `ledger_list_work_packages` detects two boundary conditions (empty project → PM, all terminal → synthesis) before entering the per-role dispatch loop.
   329	
   330	| Ledger state / action | Routes to |
   331	|---|---|
   332	| No WPs yet | `pm` (create work packages) |
   333	| `IMPLEMENT` / `REWORK` / `CONTINUE_PIPELINE` / `CLAIM_WP` / `RESUME_OR_CANCEL` | `developer` |
   334	| `RUN_QA` | `qa` |
   335	| `RUN_SECURITY_AUDIT` | `security_auditor` |
   336	| `RUN_REVIEW` | `reviewer` |
   337	| `RUN_RELEASE_ENGINEERING` / `REWORK` | `release_engineer` |
   338	| `WRITE_DOCS` / `FINALIZE_WP` / `UPDATE_CRITERIA` | `docs` |
   339	| `REPAIR_ORPHAN_BLOCKED` / `UNBLOCK_WP` / `REVIEW_*` | `pm` (PM intervention) |
   340	| All roles return `WAIT` | `synthesis` |
   341	| All WPs COMPLETE or CANCELLED | `synthesis` (final report) |
   342	| `iteration >= max_iterations` | `END` (safety limit) |
   343	| WP accumulates ≥ 3 consecutive stage failures | Circuit-breaker: WP skipped for remainder of run |
   344	
   345	For the full routing algorithm, action sets, and circuit-breaker mechanics, see [docs/supervisor-routing.md](docs/supervisor-routing.md).
   346	
   347	### Stage nodes
   348	
   349	Each stage node emits a `stage_start` event, loads a persona prompt, wraps the shared MCP tools (auto-injecting `project_path`), creates a **Deep Agent**, invokes it, and emits `stage_complete` (with `duration_s`) followed by a best-effort `pipeline_result` read-back. When dialogue capture is enabled (the default), a `dialogue_captured` event is also emitted (and appended to the run log) recording the path of the Markdown dialogue file written to disk; write failures are caught silently and do not interrupt stage execution. The 8 pipeline stages are: `pm`, `developer`, `qa`, `security_auditor`, `reviewer`, `release_engineer`, `docs`, `synthesis`. For internals, see [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).
   350	
   351	---
   352	
   353	## Folder Overview
   354	
   355	| Path | Purpose |
   356	|------|---------|
   357	| `src/supervisor.py` | Pure-Python deterministic router (no LLM calls) |
   358	| `src/graph.py` | LangGraph `StateGraph` assembly and compilation |

   418	## Troubleshooting
   419	
   420	### `MCP server error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory`
   421	
   422	The MCP server binary is not built. Run:
   423	```bash
   424	cd mcp-server && npm install && npm run build
   425	```
   426	
   427	### `Root index not found` or routing behaves unexpectedly
   428	
   429	The MCP server `dist/` is stale — compiled before a recent change to `mcp-server/src/`. Rebuild:
   430	```bash
   431	cd mcp-server && npm run build
   432	```
   433	Always rebuild after pulling commits that touch `mcp-server/src/`.
   434	
   435	### `node: command not found` when the orchestrator starts
   436	
   437	The MCP server runs as a Node.js subprocess. Ensure `node` is on your `PATH`:
   438	```bash
   439	# macOS / Linux — example (adjust path as needed)
   440	export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
   441	node --version   # should print v18 or higher
   442	```
   443	On macOS with Homebrew: `brew install node`. On Windows: use the Node.js installer from nodejs.org.
   444	
   445	### `No LLM provider API key found`
   446	
   447	Add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIza...` to `orchestrator/.env`.
   448	Install the matching extra: `pip install -e ".[anthropic]"` or `pip install -e ".[google]"`.
   449	
   450	### Checkpoint corruption (Windows)
   451	
   452	If a run crashes mid-checkpoint, delete `checkpoints/workflow.sqlite` before restarting.
   453	SQLite WAL mode reduces but does not eliminate the risk of partial writes on Windows.
   454	
   455	### `asyncio_mode` warning in pytest output
   456	
   457	This is a harmless misconfiguration warning from `pyproject.toml` — pytest-anyio reads the option but it has no effect on non-async tests.
   458	
   459	### `UserWarning: Core Pydantic V1 functionality isn't compatible with Python 3.14 or greater`
   460	
   461	This warning is emitted by `langchain-core` on every import when running Python 3.14+. It originates from `pydantic`'s internal v1 compatibility shim, which the current `langchain-core` release still imports. The warning:
   462	
   463	- **Does not affect correctness** — all tests pass and the orchestrator runs normally.
   464	- **Is not a `CompatibilityWarning`** — it is a plain `UserWarning` from `pydantic.v1`, so it cannot be silenced with `-W error::CompatibilityWarning`.
   465	- **Will resolve upstream** when `langchain-core` drops the pydantic v1 shim entirely.
   466	
   467	To suppress the noise in test output in the meantime, add the following to `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`:
   468	
   469	```toml
   470	[tool.pytest.ini_options]
   471	filterwarnings = [
   472	    "ignore::UserWarning:pydantic.v1",
   473	]
   474	```
   475	
   476	Alternatively, downgrade to Python 3.13 where pydantic's v1 shim does not emit the warning.

     2	# WP-005: Persona Build System Model Resolution Override
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	Implement configurable model settings for the persona system, replacing hardcoded YAML-only model configuration with a GUI-managed model registry and per-persona model assignment system.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Update the persona build plugin and frontmatter templates to read model assignments from `assignments.json` and `local.json` as the highest-priority override layer in the model resolution chain, and handle the "Inherit / Auto" sentinel correctly for both VS Code and Claude Code frontmatter.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `personas/plugins/ledger/index.js` — read assignments at build start, apply override in `onBuildContext` hook
    15	- `personas/plugins/ledger/frontmatter-templates.js` — make VS Code `model` field conditional (`{{#if model}}`)
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- At build start (once, cached): read `personas/model-registry/assignments.json` and `personas/model-registry/local.json`; build UUID-to-slug map from `local.json`
    20	- In `onBuildContext` hook: look up `persona_models[persona_id]` UUID in assignments, resolve to slug via UUID-to-slug map, apply as highest-priority override before existing YAML fallback logic
    21	- Resolve `default_model_slug` from `default_model_uuid` in assignments via UUID-to-slug map; override `_shared.yaml` value if found
    22	- `cc_model` resolution: look up resolved model UUID in `local.json` to get its `cc_model` field; fall back to `_shared.yaml` `cc_model` if not found
    23	- "Inherit / Auto" handling: when resolved slug is `"inherit"`, set `model` context variable to falsy (so VS Code frontmatter omits the field); set `cc_model` to `"inherit"`
    24	- VS Code frontmatter template change: `model: '{{model}}'` → `{{#if model}}model: '{{model}}'{{/if}}` — only in VS Code templates; Claude Code templates always render `model:` line
    25	- Graceful fallback: when `assignments.json` and `local.json` don't exist, fall back to current YAML-only behavior
    26	
    27	## Dependencies
    28	
    29	- WP-001
    30	
    31	## Acceptance Criteria
    32	
    33	1. The persona build system resolves models for all three suites using the priority chain: `assignments.json persona_models[persona_id]` > per-persona YAML `model`/`model_slug` > `_shared.yaml` `default_model`/`default_model_slug`
    34	2. `cc_model` is resolved per persona from the registry entry matching the assigned model UUID, falling back to `_shared.yaml` `cc_model`
    35	3. When a persona is assigned the `inherit` model, VS Code frontmatter omits the `model` field entirely
    36	4. When a persona is assigned the `inherit` model, Claude Code frontmatter uses `model: 'inherit'`
    37	5. The build functions correctly when `assignments.json` and `local.json` do not exist (graceful fallback to current YAML-only behavior)
    38	6. The `{{#if model}}` conditional is applied only to VS Code frontmatter templates — Claude Code templates always render their `model:` line
    39	
    40	## Active Pipeline Stages
    41	
    42	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    43	
    44	## Estimated Complexity
    45	
    46	Medium
    47	
    48	## Rationale
    49	
    50	The priority chain preserves YAML as fallback — users who never touch the GUI get the same behavior as today. The GUI is purely additive. UUID-to-slug resolution is performed locally by reading both files — no API dependency.
    51	
    52	## Rejected Approaches
    53	
    54	- *Boolean flag on each assignment `{ slug, inherit: true }`:* A registry entry is simpler — assignments store the sentinel UUID like any other model; consumers check `slug === 'inherit'` after resolution.
    55	- *Separate "no model" dropdown option with no registry entry:* The sentinel entry approach is more uniform — no special-case structure needed.
    56	
    57	## Notes
    58	
    59	Depends on WP-001 (registry files must exist). Can be parallelized with WP-002 through WP-009 (backend/frontend work). The `onBuildContext` hook (L96–L158 in `index.js`) runs for every persona in every suite with no suite guard — it is the single entry point for per-persona model resolution across all suites.
    60	
    61	**Code Observations:** The `onBuildContext` hook in `index.js` (L97–L157) currently handles model fallback at L117–L124: `if (!updated['model'] && updated['default_model'])`. The assignments override must be inserted before this block. The frontmatter templates in `frontmatter-templates.js` (L40–L53 for VS Code, L63–L78 for Claude Code) show that VS Code uses `model: '{{model}}'` (L44) and Claude Code uses `model: '{{cc_model}}'` via the `CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS` constant (L28). The `onSuiteInit` hook (L79–L91) conditionally applies ledger frontmatter only when `suite.personaMode === 'numbered'` — for other suites, library/config-level defaults are used. This means the `{{#if model}}` conditional needs to be applied in the config-level templates too (or the builder handles it), not just the ledger template.

Renders a header table (stage/WP ID/timestamp), per-message `## Human` / `## Assistant` / `## Tool Result` / `## System` sections, tool call JSON in fenced code blocks, and an optional token-usage footer. Returns a `str`. |

Callers passing untrusted chunk data from upstream LangGraph streams should validate values before calling this method. No-op when the writer is already closed. |

     5	
     6	Implement configurable model settings for the persona system, replacing hardcoded YAML-only model configuration with a GUI-managed model registry and per-persona model assignment system.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Update the orchestrator's `extract_persona_model_slugs()` to check `assignments.json` as the highest-priority override layer in the model resolution chain, with "inherit" slug handling and graceful fallback when assignment files are absent. Add pytest tests.
    11

    13

    15	- `orchestrator/tests/test_persona_models_assignments.py` — new test file

    18

    20	- If assignments are valid: resolve `default_model_uuid` to slug, override `_shared.yaml` default if resolved; resolve `persona_models[stage_id]` UUID to slug, override per-persona YAML if resolved

    22	- If assignments are absent or invalid: log debug message, continue with YAML-only behavior
    23	- Priority chain: resolved slug from `assignments.json persona_models[stage_id]` (skip if `"inherit"`) > per-persona YAML `model_slug` > resolved slug from `assignments.json default_model_uuid` (skip if `"inherit"`) > `_shared.yaml default_model_slug`

    31	
    32	1. The orchestrator resolves models using the priority chain: assignments > per-persona YAML > shared YAML default
